page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier, compute-leaning virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9B45 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES-NI, VAES, and SHA-NI, which accelerate cryptographic workloads and vectorized operations.

The system is equipped with 3.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-skewed ratio of 1.5 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero. Due to its compact memory footprint and low core count, total aggregate throughput is limited, although uncached memory bandwidth registers at 47.24 GB/sec for reads and 30.2 GB/sec for writes.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core tests scoring in the top 10% across evaluated systems. Single-threaded compression and decompression routines also achieve top-tier throughput, recording 37.54 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.7 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity and synthetic memory scores rank in the lower quartiles due to the 2-vCPU constraint and small 3.0 GB memory allocation. Database operations and Redis SET throughput reflect the constraints of the single physical core configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highcpu-2 offers dedicated AMD EPYC performance for workloads that prioritize per-core compute speed over broad thread parallelism or memory capacity. Primary trade-offs include the lack of local disk storage and tight memory headroom. This configuration is well matched for lightweight microservices, front-end web proxies, static web serving, single-threaded batch transformation jobs, and small utility tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-2 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning 1 physical core, 3.0 GB of memory (1.5 GB per vCPU), and 32 MB of L3 cache, with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions enabled. The configuration includes zero GPUs and no bundled local storage, relying on external network disks. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and compression efficiency, though aggregate multicore and memory performance are bounded by the low core and memory counts. Delivering strong per-thread instruction execution at an economical footprint, this instance suits lightweight microservices, static web traffic handling, CI build stages, and CPU-intensive, single-threaded processing scripts.
